412	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
413	    # Deterministic stages
414	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
415	
416	    @staticmethod
417	    def _write_int(data: bytes, pos: int, value: int, width: int,
418	                   little_endian: bool) -> bytes:
419	        """Write a (wrapped) integer of `width` bytes at `pos`."""
420	        buf = bytearray(data)
421	        mask = (1 << (8 * width)) - 1
422	        buf[pos:pos + width] = int(value & mask).to_bytes(
423	            width, "little" if little_endian else "big")
424	        return bytes(buf)
425	
426	    def _collect_token(self, tc: TestCase, pos: int, mutant: bytes) -> None:
427	        """Auto-dictionary extraction: remember a byte value whose change
428	        during the bitflip stage produced new coverage."""
429	        if len(self.auto_dict) >= MAX_AUTO_DICT_TOKENS:
430	            return
431	        token = bytes([mutant[pos]])
432	        if token not in self.auto_dict and token != tc.data[pos:pos + 1]:
433	            self.auto_dict.append(token)
434	
435	    def _bitflip_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
436	        """Walking bitflip with widths 1, 2 and 4 bits."""
437	        data = tc.data
438	        nbits = len(data) * 8
439	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
440	            for bitpos in range(0, nbits - width + 1):
441	                mutant = bit_flip(data, bitpos, width)
442	                if self.evaluate(mutant, tc) and width == 1:
443	                    self._collect_token(tc, bitpos // 8, mutant)
444	
445	    def _byte_flip_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
446	        """Walking byte flip with widths 8, 16 and 32 bits."""
447	        data = tc.data
448	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
449	            for pos in range(0, len(data) - width + 1):
450	                self.evaluate(byte_flip(data, pos, width), tc)
451	
452	    def _arithmetic_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
453	        """Arithmetic add/sub with values 1..35 for 8/16/32-bit operands
454	        (16/32-bit in both endiannesses)."""
455	        data = tc.data
456	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
457	            endianness = (False, True) if width > 1 else (False,)
458	            for pos in range(0, len(data) - width + 1):
459	                for little in endianness:
460	                    orig = int.from_bytes(data[pos:pos + width],
461	                                          "little" if little else "big")
462	                    for value in range(1, ARITH_MAX + 1):
463	                        for delta in (value, -value):
464	                            mutant = self._write_int(data, pos, orig + delta,
465	                                                     width, little)
466	                            self.evaluate(mutant, tc)
467	
468	    def _interesting_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
469	        """Interesting values 8/16/32 (16/32-bit in both endiannesses)."""
470	        data = tc.data
471	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
472	            values = INTERESTING_BY_WIDTH[width]
473	            endianness = (False, True) if width > 1 else (False,)
474	            for pos in range(0, len(data) - width + 1):
475	                for value in values:
476	                    for little in endianness:
477	                        mutant = self._write_int(data, pos, value, width,
478	                                                 little)
479	                        self.evaluate(mutant, tc)
480	
481	    def _dictionary_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
482	        """Dictionary insertion: overwrite with user + auto-dictionary
483	        tokens at every position."""
484	        data = tc.data
485	        tokens = self.user_dict + self.auto_dict
486	        for pos in range(len(data)):
487	            for token in tokens:
488	                if len(token) > len(data) - pos:
489	                    continue
490	                mutant = data[:pos] + token + data[pos + len(token):]
491	                self.evaluate(mutant, tc)
492	
493	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
494	    # Havoc and splice
495	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
496	
497	    def _stack_havoc(self, data: bytes) -> bytes:
498	        """Apply 2^1..2^7 stacked random mutations (AFL havoc)."""
499	        buf = bytearray(data)
500	        num_ops = 1 << self.rng.randint(1, 8)
501	        for _ in range(num_ops):
502	            if not buf:
503	                buf = bytearray(b"\x00")
504	            pos = self.rng.randint(0, len(buf))
505	            op = self.rng.randint(0, 12)
506	            if op == 0:  # bit flip
507	                buf[pos] ^= 1 << self.rng.randint(0, 8)
508	            elif op == 1:  # interesting 8-bit value
509	                buf[pos] = INTERESTING_8[
510	                    self.rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_8))] & 0xFF
511	            elif op == 2:  # arithmetic add
512	                buf[pos] = (buf[pos] + self.rng.randint(1, ARITH_MAX + 1)) \
513	                    & 0xFF
514	            elif op == 3:  # arithmetic sub
515	                buf[pos] = (buf[pos] - self.rng.randint(1, ARITH_MAX + 1)) \
516	                    & 0xFF
517	            elif op == 4:  # random byte
518	                buf[pos] = self.rng.randint(0, 256)
519	            elif op == 5:  # delete bytes
520	                if len(buf) > 1:
521	                    length = self.rng.randint(1, len(buf))
522	                    del buf[pos:pos + length]
523	            elif op == 6:  # clone bytes
524	                if len(buf) > 1:
525	                    src = self.rng.randint(0, len(buf))
526	                    length = self.rng.randint(1, len(buf) - src + 1)
527	                    buf[pos:pos + length] = buf[src:src + length]
528	            elif op == 7:  # insert random bytes
529	                length = self.rng.randint(1, 9)
530	                chunk = bytes(
531	                    self.rng.randint(0, 256, size=length).astype(np.uint8))
532	                buf[pos:pos] = chunk
533	            elif op == 8:  # overwrite with random bytes
534	                length = self.rng.randint(1, len(buf) - pos + 1)
535	                chunk = bytes(
536	                    self.rng.randint(0, 256, size=length).astype(np.uint8))
537	                buf[pos:pos + length] = chunk
538	            elif op in (9, 10):  # interesting 16-bit value, LE / BE
539	                if len(buf) - pos >= 2:
540	                    value = INTERESTING_16[
541	                        self.rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_16))]
542	                    buf[pos:pos + 2] = int(value & 0xFFFF).to_bytes(
543	                        2, "little" if op == 9 else "big")
544	            else:  # interesting 32-bit value, random endianness
545	                if len(buf) - pos >= 4:
546	                    value = INTERESTING_32[
547	                        self.rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_32))]
548	                    little = bool(self.rng.randint(0, 2))
549	                    buf[pos:pos + 4] = int(value & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(
550	                        4, "little" if little else "big")
551	            if len(buf) > self.max_input_len:
552	                del buf[self.max_input_len:]
553	        return bytes(buf)
554	
555	    def _havoc_stage(self, tc: TestCase, energy: int) -> None:
556	        """Havoc stage: `energy` iterations of stacked random mutations."""
557	        for _ in range(energy):
558	            self.evaluate(self._stack_havoc(tc.data), tc)
559	
560	    def _splice_stage(self, tc: TestCase, energy: int) -> None:
561	        """Splice stage: combine two queue entries at a midpoint, then
562	        run the result through havoc."""
563	        if len(self.queue) < 2:
564	            return
565	        for _ in range(energy):
566	            other = self.queue[self.rng.randint(0, len(self.queue))]
567	            if other is tc:
568	                continue
569	            mutant = splice(tc.data, other.data, self.rng)
570	            self.evaluate(self._stack_havoc(mutant), tc)
571	
572	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
573	    # Scheduling / main loop
574	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
575	
576	    def fuzz_one(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
577	        """Run the full AFL pipeline on one queue entry."""
578	        tc.times_chosen += 1
579	        tc.fuzz_count += 1
580	        if not tc.was_fuzzed:
581	            if self.enable_trimming:
582	                self.trim_case(tc)
583	            self._bitflip_stage(tc)
584	            self._byte_flip_stage(tc)
585	            self._arithmetic_stage(tc)
586	            self._interesting_stage(tc)
587	            self._dictionary_stage(tc)
588	            tc.was_fuzzed = True
589	        self.calculate_score(tc)
590	        self._havoc_stage(tc, self.assign_energy(tc))
591	        if self.current_cycle >= 1:
592	            self._splice_stage(tc, self.splice_energy)
593	
594	    def run(self, max_cycles: Optional[int] = None,
595	            max_execs: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
596	        """Main fuzzing loop.
597	
598	        Cycles through the queue in order; entries discovered during a
599	        cycle are scheduled from the next cycle onward. Non-favored seeds
600	        are skipped with probability ``skip_nonfavored_prob`` (75/25
601	        favored priority). The queue is re-culled after every cycle.
602	        """
603	        cycle = 0
604	        while max_cycles is None or cycle < max_cycles:
605	            self.current_cycle = cycle
606	            snapshot = list(self.queue)
607	            for tc in snapshot:
608	                if (max_execs is not None
609	                        and self.fork_server.exec_count >= max_execs):
610	                    self.cull_queue()
611	                    return
612	                has_favored = any(t.is_favored for t in self.queue)
613	                if (not tc.is_favored and has_favored
614	                        and self.rng.rand() < self.skip_nonfavored_prob):
615	                    continue
616	                self.fuzz_one(tc)
617	            self.cull_queue()
618	            cycle += 1

2	title: "AFLFast: Power Schedules via Markov Chain Model"
3	description: |
4	  Implement AFLFast's power schedules based on modeling fuzzing as a Markov chain.
5	  Each unique execution path is a state; mutations cause transitions between states.
6	  The key insight is that AFL's constant energy wastes effort on high-frequency paths.
7	  AFLFast assigns energy inversely proportional to path frequency f(i) and exponentially
8	  in selection count s(i). Includes: EXPLOIT schedule (p(i)=alpha, same as AFL),
9	  EXPLORE schedule (p(i)=alpha/beta, normalized), COE schedule (cut-off exponential:
10	  skip seeds with f(i)>mu, otherwise min(alpha/beta * 2^s(i), M)), FAST schedule
11	  (recommended: min(alpha/beta * 2^s(i) / f(i), M)), LINEAR schedule (min(alpha/beta *
12	  s(i)/f(i), M)), QUAD schedule (min(alpha/beta * s(i)^2/f(i), M)). Also implements
13	  PathFrequencyTracker (Markov state identification, transition counting, rare path
14	  detection), seed prioritization strategies (prioritize_small_s for FAST/COE,
15	  prioritize_small_f for explore/linear/quad), EnergyComputer with Gini coefficient
16	  analysis, and schedule comparison utilities.

2	
3	Properties:
4	- 20 basic blocks, 30 edges
5	- Multiple execution paths of varying depth
6	- 2 crash paths (require specific multi-byte sequences)
7	- Some rare edges (require specific byte values)
8	- Known shortest distances from each block to target blocks
9	"""
10	
11	from fuzzsim.program_model import SimulatedProgram, BasicBlock, Edge
12	from typing import Tuple, Set, Dict
13	import numpy as np
14	
15	
16	def build_crashme() -> SimulatedProgram:
17	    """Build the 'crashme' simulated program.
18	
19	    CFG structure (20 blocks, 30 edges):
20	    Block 0 (entry) -> Block 1 (byte[0] % 3 == 0)
21	                    -> Block 2 (byte[0] % 3 == 1)
22	                    -> Block 3 (byte[0] % 3 == 2)
23	
24	    Block 1 -> Block 4, Block 5
25	    Block 2 -> Block 6, Block 7
26	    Block 3 -> Block 8, Block 9
27	
28	    Block 4 -> Block 10, Block 11
29	    Block 5 -> Block 12
30	    Block 6 -> Block 13, Block 14
31	    Block 7 -> Block 15
32	    Block 8 -> Block 16, Block 17  (Block 17 = crash path 1 entry)
33	    Block 9 -> Block 18
34	
35	    Block 10 -> Block 19 (exit)
36	    Block 11 -> Block 19
37	    Block 12 -> Block 19
38	    Block 13 -> Block 19
39	    Block 14 -> Block 15 (rare edge)
40	    Block 15 -> Block 19
41	    Block 16 -> Block 19
42	    Block 17 -> Block 19 (crash edge!)
43	    Block 18 -> Block 17 (crash path 2 entry, rare)
44	    Block 19 (exit, no outgoing)
45	
46	    Target blocks: [17, 19]
47	    """
48	    blocks = [BasicBlock(i) for i in range(20)]
49	
50	    edges = [
51	        # From entry block 0
52	        Edge(0, 0, 1),
53	        Edge(1, 0, 2),
54	        Edge(2, 0, 3),
55	        # From block 1
56	        Edge(3, 1, 4),
57	        Edge(4, 1, 5),
58	        # From block 2
59	        Edge(5, 2, 6),
60	        Edge(6, 2, 7),
61	        # From block 3
62	        Edge(7, 3, 8),
63	        Edge(8, 3, 9),
64	        # From block 4
65	        Edge(9, 4, 10),
66	        Edge(10, 4, 11),
67	        # From block 5
68	        Edge(11, 5, 12),
69	        # From block 6
70	        Edge(12, 6, 13),
71	        Edge(13, 6, 14, is_rare=True),
72	        # From block 7
73	        Edge(14, 7, 15),
74	        # From block 8
75	        Edge(15, 8, 16),
76	        Edge(16, 8, 17, is_rare=True),  # rare: requires specific bytes
77	        # From block 9
78	        Edge(17, 9, 18),
79	        # From block 10
80	        Edge(18, 10, 19),
81	        # From block 11
82	        Edge(19, 11, 19),
83	        # From block 12
84	        Edge(20, 12, 19),
85	        # From block 13
86	        Edge(21, 13, 19),
87	        # From block 14
88	        Edge(22, 14, 15, is_rare=True),
89	        # From block 15
90	        Edge(23, 15, 19),
91	        # From block 16
92	        Edge(24, 16, 19),
93	        # From block 17 (crash!)
94	        Edge(25, 17, 19, is_crash=True),
95	        # From block 18
96	        Edge(26, 18, 17, is_rare=True),  # rare path to crash
97	        # Additional edges for more complex paths
98	        Edge(27, 5, 4),   # back edge for loop
99	        Edge(28, 12, 6),  # back edge
100	        Edge(29, 16, 8),  # back edge
101	    ]
102	
103	    target_blocks = [17, 19]
104	
105	    program = SimulatedProgram(blocks, edges, entry_block=0,
106	                               target_blocks=target_blocks)
107	    return program

110	class CrashmeProgram:
111	    """Wrapper around SimulatedProgram with crashme-specific execution logic.
112	
113	    Uses a more sophisticated execution model where specific byte sequences
114	    are needed to trigger certain paths.
115	    """
116	
117	    def __init__(self):
118	        self.program = build_crashme()
119	        self.total_edges = len(self.program.edges)
120	        self.total_blocks = len(self.program.blocks)
121	
122	    def execute(self, input_data: bytes) -> Tuple[Set[int], bool, float]:
123	        """Execute crashme with input-dependent path selection.
124	
125	        Path selection logic:
126	        - Byte 0: selects initial branch (mod 3)
127	        - Byte 1: selects second-level branch (mod 2)
128	        - Byte 2+: selects deeper branches with specific conditions
129	
130	        Crash path 1: byte[0]%3==2, byte[1]%2==0, byte[2] in [0x30..0x3F],
131	                       byte[3] in [0x80..0x9F]
132	          -> blocks 0,3,8,17,19 (crash edge 25)
133	        Crash path 2: byte[0]%3==2, byte[1]%2==1, byte[2]==0x4D,
134	                       byte[3]==0x5A, byte[4]%4==3
135	          -> blocks 0,3,9,18,17,19 (crash edge 25 via rare 26)
136	        """
137	        edges_hit = set()
138	        is_crash = False
139	        exec_time = 0.001  # base cost
140	
141	        if len(input_data) == 0:
142	            return edges_hit, False, exec_time
143	
144	        # Level 1: entry -> {1, 2, 3}
145	        b0 = input_data[0] if len(input_data) > 0 else 0
146	        branch1 = b0 % 3
147	
148	        if branch1 == 0:
149	            edges_hit.add(0)  # 0->1
150	            current = 1
151	        elif branch1 == 1:
152	            edges_hit.add(1)  # 0->2
153	            current = 2
154	        else:
155	            edges_hit.add(2)  # 0->3
156	            current = 3
157	
158	        exec_time += 0.001
159	
160	        # Level 2
161	        b1 = input_data[1] if len(input_data) > 1 else 0
162	        branch2 = b1 % 2
163	
164	        if current == 1:
165	            if branch2 == 0:
166	                edges_hit.add(3)  # 1->4
167	                current = 4
168	            else:
169	                edges_hit.add(4)  # 1->5
170	                current = 5
171	        elif current == 2:
172	            if branch2 == 0:
173	                edges_hit.add(5)  # 2->6
174	                current = 6
175	            else:
176	                edges_hit.add(6)  # 2->7
177	                current = 7
178	        elif current == 3:
179	            if branch2 == 0:
180	                edges_hit.add(7)  # 3->8
181	                current = 8
182	            else:
183	                edges_hit.add(8)  # 3->9
184	                current = 9
185	
186	        exec_time += 0.001
187	
188	        # Level 3
189	        b2 = input_data[2] if len(input_data) > 2 else 0
190	        b3 = input_data[3] if len(input_data) > 3 else 0
191	        b4 = input_data[4] if len(input_data) > 4 else 0
192	        b5 = input_data[5] if len(input_data) > 5 else 0
193	
194	        if current == 4:
195	            if b2 % 2 == 0:
196	                edges_hit.add(9)   # 4->10
197	                edges_hit.add(18)  # 10->19
198	            else:
199	                edges_hit.add(10)  # 4->11
200	                edges_hit.add(19)  # 11->19
201	        elif current == 5:
202	            edges_hit.add(11)  # 5->12
203	            # Loop: if byte[3] is high, take back edge
204	            if b3 > 200:
205	                edges_hit.add(27)  # 5->4 back edge
206	                edges_hit.add(9)   # 4->10
207	                edges_hit.add(18)  # 10->19
208	            else:
209	                edges_hit.add(20)  # 12->19
210	        elif current == 6:
211	            if b2 % 8 == 7:  # rare condition (1/8 chance)
212	                edges_hit.add(13)  # 6->14 (rare)
213	                edges_hit.add(22)  # 14->15 (rare)
214	                edges_hit.add(23)  # 15->19
215	            else:
216	                edges_hit.add(12)  # 6->13
217	                edges_hit.add(21)  # 13->19
218	        elif current == 7:
219	            edges_hit.add(14)  # 7->15
220	            edges_hit.add(23)  # 15->19
221	        elif current == 8:
222	            # Crash path 1: requires byte[2] in [0x30..0x3F] AND byte[3] in [0x80..0x9F]
223	            if 0x30 <= b2 <= 0x3F and 0x80 <= b3 <= 0x9F:
224	                edges_hit.add(16)  # 8->17 (rare)
225	                edges_hit.add(25)  # 17->19 (CRASH!)
226	                is_crash = True
227	            else:
228	                edges_hit.add(15)  # 8->16
229	                # Loop back edge possibility
230	                if b3 > 200 and b4 > 200:
231	                    edges_hit.add(29)  # 16->8 back edge
232	                    edges_hit.add(15)  # 8->16 again
233	                edges_hit.add(24)  # 16->19
234	        elif current == 9:
235	            edges_hit.add(17)  # 9->18
236	            # Crash path 2: requires byte[2]==0x4D, byte[3]==0x5A, byte[4]%4==3
237	            if b2 == 0x4D and b3 == 0x5A and b4 % 4 == 3:
238	                edges_hit.add(26)  # 18->17 (rare)
239	                edges_hit.add(25)  # 17->19 (CRASH!)
240	                is_crash = True
241	
242	        exec_time += 0.001 * len(edges_hit)
243	        return edges_hit, is_crash, exec_time
244	
245	    def get_total_edges(self) -> int:
246	        return self.total_edges
247	
248	    def get_crash_edges(self) -> Set[int]:
249	        return self.program.get_crash_edges()
250	
251	    def get_rare_edges(self) -> Set[int]:
252	        return self.program.get_rare_edges()
253	
254	    def get_target_blocks(self):
255	        return self.program.target_blocks
256	
257	    def get_distances(self, target_blocks=None) -> Dict[int, float]:
258	        if target_blocks is None:
259	            target_blocks = self.program.target_blocks
260	        return self.program.get_shortest_distances(target_blocks)

9	- test case calibration (multi-run stability detection, average exec time)
10	- input trimming (powers-of-two block removal preserving coverage)
11	- corpus culling via greedy set cover (smallest+fastest seed per edge)
12	- full deterministic stages in AFL order: walking bitflip 1/2/4 bits,
13	  byte flip 8/16/32 bits, arithmetic add/sub 1..35 for 8/16/32-bit widths
14	  (both endianness), interesting values 8/16/32 (both endianness),
15	  dictionary insertion (user tokens + auto-dictionary extracted during the
16	  bitflip stage when a byte value change produced new coverage)
17	- havoc stage with 2^1..2^7 stacked random mutations per iteration
18	- splice stage (midpoint combination of two queue entries, then havoc)
19	- performance scoring (``calculate_score``) from exec speed, coverage size,
20	  depth and stability
21	- constant power schedule (fixed energy per seed, AFL-style)
22	- crash deduplication via coverage hash (hash of the crashing edge set)
23	- queue scheduling with favored-seed priority (75% skip of non-favored
24	  seeds, 25% fuzz them anyway)
25	
26	All randomness flows through a single ``np.random.RandomState`` instance so
27	runs are fully deterministic given the seed.
28	"""
29

31	from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set

36	from fuzzsim.mutation import (
37	    INTERESTING_8,
38	    INTERESTING_16,
39	    INTERESTING_32,
40	    bit_flip,
41	    byte_flip,
42	    splice,

46	ARITH_MAX = 35  # AFL arithmetic stage uses values 1..35
47	SKIP_NONFAVORED_PROB = 0.75  # 75% chance to skip a non-favored seed
48	CALIBRATION_RUNS = 3  # calibration executions per new test case
49	MAX_AUTO_DICT_TOKENS = 128  # cap on auto-extracted dictionary tokens
50	
51	# Interesting value tables per operand width (in bytes), as in AFL.
52	INTERESTING_BY_WIDTH = {
53	    1: INTERESTING_8,
54	    2: INTERESTING_16,
55	    4: INTERESTING_32,
56	}

59	def classify_counts(counts: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
60	    """Bucket raw hit counts the way AFL's ``classify_counts`` does.
61	
62	    Buckets: 1, 2, 3, 4-7, 8-15, 16-31, 32-127, 128+. Zero stays zero.
63	    The bucket id reported for a range is the range's lower bound encoded
64	    as in AFL's bucket shift table (1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 respectively).
65	    """
66	    counts = np.asarray(counts)
67	    out = np.zeros(counts.shape, dtype=np.uint8)
68	    out[counts == 1] = 1
69	    out[counts == 2] = 2
70	    out[counts == 3] = 3
71	    out[(counts >= 4) & (counts <= 7)] = 4
72	    out[(counts >= 8) & (counts <= 15)] = 5
73	    out[(counts >= 16) & (counts <= 31)] = 6
74	    out[(counts >= 32) & (counts <= 127)] = 7
75	    out[counts >= 128] = 8
76	    return out

79	def edge_hash(prev_block: int, cur_block: int) -> int:
80	    """Hash a CFG edge into the 64KB bitmap: (prev XOR cur) >> 1."""
81	    return ((prev_block ^ cur_block) >> 1) % MAP_SIZE

84	class ForkServerResult:
85	    """Result of a single fork-server execution."""
86	
87	    __slots__ = ("edges", "classified", "is_crash", "exec_time")
88	
89	    def __init__(self, edges: Set[int], classified: np.ndarray,
90	                 is_crash: bool, exec_time: float):
91	        self.edges = edges
92	        self.classified = classified  # bucketed 64KB bitmap (np.uint8 array)
93	        self.is_crash = is_crash
94	        self.exec_time = exec_time

97	class ForkServer:
98	    """Simulates AFL's fork server.
99	
100	    Executes the target on demand, keeps an execution counter, and reports
101	    coverage both as an exact edge set and as a classified 64KB bitmap
102	    (edge ids are mapped into the bitmap via ``edge_hash`` when the target
103	    exposes CFG block information, otherwise by edge id).
104	    """
105	
106	    def __init__(self, target):
107	        self.target = target
108	        self.exec_count = 0
109	        self._edge_index: Dict[int, int] = {}
110	        program = getattr(target, "program", None)
111	        if program is not None:
112	            for edge in program.edges:
113	                self._edge_index[edge.edge_id] = edge_hash(edge.src, edge.dst)
114	
115	    def bitmap_index(self, edge_id: int) -> int:
116	        """Return the bitmap index for an edge id."""
117	        return self._edge_index.get(edge_id, edge_id % MAP_SIZE)
118	
119	    def run(self, data: bytes) -> ForkServerResult:
120	        """Execute the target once and classify the hit counts."""
121	        self.exec_count += 1
122	        edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.target.execute(data)
123	        counts = np.zeros(MAP_SIZE, dtype=np.uint8)
124	        for edge_id in edges:
125	            idx = self.bitmap_index(edge_id)
126	            counts[idx] = min(255, counts[idx] + 1)
127	        return ForkServerResult(edges, classify_counts(counts),
128	                                is_crash, exec_time)

131	class AFLFuzzer:
132	    """Core AFL fuzzer driving a simulated target.
133	
134	    Parameters:
135	        target: program under test (must provide ``execute(bytes)``).
136	        seeds: initial corpus inputs.
137	        rng: ``np.random.RandomState`` used for ALL randomness.
138	        havoc_energy: fixed energy (havoc iterations) per scheduled seed;
139	            this is the constant power schedule.
140	        splice_energy: splice iterations per scheduled seed (from cycle 1).
141	        max_input_len: cap on mutated input length.
142	        enable_trimming: run powers-of-two trimming before deterministic
143	            stages (AFL default behavior; can be disabled per experiment).
144	        calibration_runs: executions per calibration.
145	        skip_nonfavored_prob: probability of skipping a non-favored seed.
146	    """
147	
148	    def __init__(self, target, seeds: List[bytes],
149	                 rng: Optional[np.random.RandomState] = None,
150	                 havoc_energy: int = 16, splice_energy: int = 4,
151	                 max_input_len: int = 1024, enable_trimming: bool = True,
152	                 calibration_runs: int = CALIBRATION_RUNS,
153	                 skip_nonfavored_prob: float = SKIP_NONFAVORED_PROB):
154	        self.target = target
155	        self.rng = rng if rng is not None else np.random.RandomState(0)
156	        self.havoc_energy = havoc_energy
157	        self.splice_energy = splice_energy
158	        self.max_input_len = max_input_len
159	        self.enable_trimming = enable_trimming
160	        self.calibration_runs = calibration_runs
161	        self.skip_nonfavored_prob = skip_nonfavored_prob
162	
163	        self.fork_server = ForkServer(target)
164	        self.bitmap = CoverageBitmap()
165	        # OR of all admitted classified bitmaps: a bucket pattern counts as
166	        # "new coverage" if it sets a byte never seen before.
167	        self._seen_classified = np.zeros(MAP_SIZE, dtype=np.uint8)
168	
169	        self.queue: List[TestCase] = []
170	        self.crashes: Dict[str, TestCase] = {}  # coverage hash -> crash TC
171	        self.user_dict: List[bytes] = []
172	        self.auto_dict: List[bytes] = []
173	        self.current_cycle = 0
174	        self.scores: Dict[int, float] = {}  # id(tc) -> calculate_score value
175	
176	        for seed in seeds:
177	            self._load_initial_seed(seed)
178	        self.cull_queue()
179	
180	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
181	    # Corpus / reporting properties
182	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
183	
184	    @property
185	    def paths_discovered(self) -> int:
186	        """Total number of queue entries (paths) discovered."""
187	        return len(self.queue)
188	
189	    @property
190	    def corpus_size(self) -> int:
191	        """Corpus size after culling bookkeeping (culling marks favored
192	        seeds but never removes entries, so this equals paths)."""
193	        return len(self.queue)
194	
195	    @property
196	    def unique_crashes(self) -> int:
197	        """Number of deduplicated crashes."""
198	        return len(self.crashes)
199	
200	    @property
201	    def exec_count(self) -> int:
202	        return self.fork_server.exec_count
203	
204	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
205	    # Calibration, trimming, culling
206	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
207	
208	    def calibrate_case(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
209	        """Run a test case multiple times to measure stability.
210	
211	        Stores the average execution time and flags the case as variable
212	        if the classified coverage differs between runs.
213	        """
214	        signatures = []
215	        times = []
216	        for _ in range(self.calibration_runs):
217	            res = self.fork_server.run(tc.data)
218	            signatures.append(res.classified.tobytes())
219	            times.append(res.exec_time)
220	        tc.exec_time = sum(times) / len(times) if times else 0.0
221	        # Dynamic attribute: TestCase has no stability field of its own.
222	        tc.is_variable = len(set(signatures)) > 1  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
223	
224	    def trim_case(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
225	        """Powers-of-two block removal trimming.
226	
227	        Try removing blocks of size len/2, len/4, ... down to 1 byte. A
228	        removal is kept only if the classified coverage is preserved.
229	        """
230	        data = tc.data
231	        if len(data) < 5:
232	            return
233	        reference = self.fork_server.run(data)
234	        if reference.is_crash:
235	            return
236	        ref_sig = reference.classified.tobytes()
237	
238	        shift = 1
239	        while (len(data) >> shift) >= 1:
240	            block = len(data) >> shift
241	            pos = 0
242	            while pos < len(data):
243	                end = min(pos + block, len(data))
244	                candidate = data[:pos] + data[end:]
245	                if candidate:
246	                    res = self.fork_server.run(candidate)
247	                    if (not res.is_crash
248	                            and res.classified.tobytes() == ref_sig):
249	                        data = candidate
250	                        continue  # retry at same position with shifted data
251	                pos += block
252	            shift += 1
253	        if data != tc.data:
254	            tc.data = data
255	
256	    def cull_queue(self) -> None:
257	        """Greedy set cover: for each covered edge pick the smallest and
258	        fastest queue entry covering it. Those entries are marked favored
259	        and their ``unique_edges`` set is updated."""
260	        best_for_edge: Dict[int, TestCase] = {}
261	        for edge_id in sorted(self.bitmap.global_coverage):
262	            best: Optional[TestCase] = None
263	            for tc in self.queue:
264	                if edge_id in tc.coverage:
265	                    if (best is None
266	                            or (tc.size, tc.exec_time) < (best.size,
267	                                                          best.exec_time)):
268	                        best = tc
269	            if best is not None:
270	                best_for_edge[edge_id] = best
271	
272	        favored = set(best_for_edge.values())
273	        for tc in self.queue:
274	            tc.is_favored = tc in favored
275	            tc.unique_edges = {e for e, b in best_for_edge.items() if b is tc}
276	
277	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
278	    # Scoring and power schedule
279	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
280	
281	    def calculate_score(self, tc: TestCase) -> float:
282	        """AFL-style performance score based on exec speed, coverage size,
283	        depth and stability. Higher is better."""
284	        if not self.queue:
285	            return 100.0
286	        avg_exec = sum(t.exec_time for t in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
287	        avg_cov = sum(len(t.coverage) for t in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
288	
289	        score = 100.0
290	        # Execution speed relative to the corpus average.
291	        if avg_exec > 0:
292	            ratio = tc.exec_time / avg_exec
293	            if ratio > 10:
294	                score *= 0.25
295	            elif ratio > 4:
296	                score *= 0.5
297	            elif ratio > 2:
298	                score *= 0.75
299	            elif ratio < 0.25:
300	                score *= 3.0
301	            elif ratio < 0.5:
302	                score *= 2.0
303	            elif ratio < 0.75:
304	                score *= 1.5
305	        # Coverage size relative to the corpus average.
306	        if avg_cov > 0:
307	            cratio = len(tc.coverage) / avg_cov
308	            if cratio > 3:
309	                score *= 4.0
310	            elif cratio > 2:
311	                score *= 3.0
312	            elif cratio > 1.5:
313	                score *= 2.0
314	            elif cratio < 0.25:
315	                score *= 0.25
316	            elif cratio < 0.5:
317	                score *= 0.5
318	            elif cratio < 0.75:
319	                score *= 0.75
320	        # Depth handicap: deeper inputs get less energy in AFL.
321	        if tc.depth > 3:
322	            score *= 0.8 ** min(tc.depth - 3, 8)
323	        # Stability: variable inputs are de-prioritized.
324	        if getattr(tc, "is_variable", False):
325	            score *= 0.5
326	
327	        self.scores[id(tc)] = score
328	        return score
329	
330	    def assign_energy(self, tc: TestCase) -> int:
331	        """Constant power schedule: every seed gets the same fixed energy."""
332	        return self.havoc_energy

334	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
335	    # Evaluation / queue admission / crash dedup
336	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
337	
338	    @staticmethod
339	    def crash_hash(edges: Set[int]) -> str:
340	        """Deduplication hash of a crashing edge set."""
341	        payload = ",".join(str(e) for e in sorted(edges)).encode()
342	        return hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
343	
344	    def _has_new_tuple(self, classified: np.ndarray) -> bool:
345	        """Check the classified bitmap for never-before-seen buckets."""
346	        return bool(np.any((classified > 0) & (self._seen_classified == 0)))
347	
348	    def _record_crash(self, data: bytes, res: ForkServerResult) -> bool:
349	        """Store a crash if its coverage hash has not been seen."""
350	        h = self.crash_hash(res.edges)
351	        if h in self.crashes:
352	            return False
353	        tc = TestCase(data=data, coverage=set(res.edges),
354	                      exec_time=res.exec_time, is_crash=True,
355	                      creation_time=self.fork_server.exec_count)
356	        self.crashes[h] = tc
357	        return True
358	
359	    def evaluate(self, data: bytes, parent: TestCase) -> bool:
360	        """Execute a candidate input; queue it on new coverage.
361	
362	        Crashes are deduplicated by coverage hash and never queued, but
363	        their coverage is folded into the global bitmap. Returns True if
364	        the input was added to the queue.
365	        """
366	        if not data:
367	            return False
368	        res = self.fork_server.run(data)
369	        if res.is_crash:
370	            self._record_crash(data, res)
371	            self.bitmap.update(res.edges)
372	            self._seen_classified |= res.classified
373	            return False
374	
375	        new_edges = res.edges - self.bitmap.global_coverage
376	        if not new_edges and not self._has_new_tuple(res.classified):
377	            return False
378	
379	        self.bitmap.update(res.edges)
380	        self._seen_classified |= res.classified
381	        tc = TestCase(
382	            data=data,
383	            coverage=set(res.edges),
384	            exec_time=res.exec_time,
385	            depth=parent.depth + 1,
386	            creation_time=self.fork_server.exec_count,
387	        )
388	        self.calibrate_case(tc)
389	        self.queue.append(tc)
390	        return True
391	
392	    def _load_initial_seed(self, data: bytes) -> None:
393	        """Add an initial seed to the queue (calibrated, deduplicating
394	        crashes). Like AFL, initial seeds are queued even if another seed
395	        already covers the same edges."""
396	        res = self.fork_server.run(data)
397	        self.bitmap.update(res.edges)
398	        self._seen_classified |= res.classified
399	        if res.is_crash:
400	            self._record_crash(data, res)
401	            return
402	        tc = TestCase(
403	            data=data,
404	            coverage=set(res.edges),
405	            exec_time=res.exec_time,
406	            depth=0,
407	            creation_time=self.fork_server.exec_count,
408	        )
409	        self.calibrate_case(tc)
410	        self.queue.append(tc)

412	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
413	    # Deterministic stages
414	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
415	
416	    @staticmethod
417	    def _write_int(data: bytes, pos: int, value: int, width: int,
418	                   little_endian: bool) -> bytes:
419	        """Write a (wrapped) integer of `width` bytes at `pos`."""
420	        buf = bytearray(data)
421	        mask = (1 << (8 * width)) - 1
422	        buf[pos:pos + width] = int(value & mask).to_bytes(
423	            width, "little" if little_endian else "big")
424	        return bytes(buf)
425	
426	    def _collect_token(self, tc: TestCase, pos: int, mutant: bytes) -> None:
427	        """Auto-dictionary extraction: remember a byte value whose change
428	        during the bitflip stage produced new coverage."""
429	        if len(self.auto_dict) >= MAX_AUTO_DICT_TOKENS:
430	            return
431	        token = bytes([mutant[pos]])
432	        if token not in self.auto_dict and token != tc.data[pos:pos + 1]:
433	            self.auto_dict.append(token)
434	
435	    def _bitflip_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
436	        """Walking bitflip with widths 1, 2 and 4 bits."""
437	        data = tc.data
438	        nbits = len(data) * 8
439	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
440	            for bitpos in range(0, nbits - width + 1):
441	                mutant = bit_flip(data, bitpos, width)
442	                if self.evaluate(mutant, tc) and width == 1:
443	                    self._collect_token(tc, bitpos // 8, mutant)
444	
445	    def _byte_flip_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
446	        """Walking byte flip with widths 8, 16 and 32 bits."""
447	        data = tc.data
448	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
449	            for pos in range(0, len(data) - width + 1):
450	                self.evaluate(byte_flip(data, pos, width), tc)
451	
452	    def _arithmetic_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
453	        """Arithmetic add/sub with values 1..35 for 8/16/32-bit operands
454	        (16/32-bit in both endiannesses)."""
455	        data = tc.data
456	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
457	            endianness = (False, True) if width > 1 else (False,)
458	            for pos in range(0, len(data) - width + 1):
459	                for little in endianness:
460	                    orig = int.from_bytes(data[pos:pos + width],
461	                                          "little" if little else "big")
462	                    for value in range(1, ARITH_MAX + 1):
463	                        for delta in (value, -value):
464	                            mutant = self._write_int(data, pos, orig + delta,
465	                                                     width, little)
466	                            self.evaluate(mutant, tc)
467	
468	    def _interesting_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
469	        """Interesting values 8/16/32 (16/32-bit in both endiannesses)."""
470	        data = tc.data
471	        for width in (1, 2, 4):
472	            values = INTERESTING_BY_WIDTH[width]
473	            endianness = (False, True) if width > 1 else (False,)
474	            for pos in range(0, len(data) - width + 1):
475	                for value in values:
476	                    for little in endianness:
477	                        mutant = self._write_int(data, pos, value, width,
478	                                                 little)
479	                        self.evaluate(mutant, tc)
480	
481	    def _dictionary_stage(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
482	        """Dictionary insertion: overwrite with user + auto-dictionary
483	        tokens at every position."""
484	        data = tc.data
485	        tokens = self.user_dict + self.auto_dict
486	        for pos in range(len(data)):
487	            for token in tokens:
488	                if len(token) > len(data) - pos:
489	                    continue
490	                mutant = data[:pos] + token + data[pos + len(token):]
491	                self.evaluate(mutant, tc)
492	
493	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
494	    # Havoc and splice
495	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
496	
497	    def _stack_havoc(self, data: bytes) -> bytes:
498	        """Apply 2^1..2^7 stacked random mutations (AFL havoc)."""
499	        buf = bytearray(data)
500	        num_ops = 1 << self.rng.randint(1, 8)
501	        for _ in range(num_ops):
502	            if not buf:
503	                buf = bytearray(b"\x00")
504	            pos = self.rng.randint(0, len(buf))
505	            op = self.rng.randint(0, 12)
506	            if op == 0:  # bit flip
507	                buf[pos] ^= 1 << self.rng.randint(0, 8)
508	            elif op == 1:  # interesting 8-bit value
509	                buf[pos] = INTERESTING_8[
510	                    self.rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_8))] & 0xFF
511	            elif op == 2:  # arithmetic add
512	                buf[pos] = (buf[pos] + self.rng.randint(1, ARITH_MAX + 1)) \
513	                    & 0xFF
514	            elif op == 3:  # arithmetic sub
515	                buf[pos] = (buf[pos] - self.rng.randint(1, ARITH_MAX + 1)) \
516	                    & 0xFF
517	            elif op == 4:  # random byte
518	                buf[pos] = self.rng.randint(0, 256)
519	            elif op == 5:  # delete bytes
520	                if len(buf) > 1:
521	                    length = self.rng.randint(1, len(buf))
522	                    del buf[pos:pos + length]
523	            elif op == 6:  # clone bytes
524	                if len(buf) > 1:
525	                    src = self.rng.randint(0, len(buf))
526	                    length = self.rng.randint(1, len(buf) - src + 1)
527	                    buf[pos:pos + length] = buf[src:src + length]
528	            elif op == 7:  # insert random bytes
529	                length = self.rng.randint(1, 9)
530	                chunk = bytes(
531	                    self.rng.randint(0, 256, size=length).astype(np.uint8))
532	                buf[pos:pos] = chunk
533	            elif op == 8:  # overwrite with random bytes
534	                length = self.rng.randint(1, len(buf) - pos + 1)
535	                chunk = bytes(
536	                    self.rng.randint(0, 256, size=length).astype(np.uint8))
537	                buf[pos:pos + length] = chunk
538	            elif op in (9, 10):  # interesting 16-bit value, LE / BE
539	                if len(buf) - pos >= 2:
540	                    value = INTERESTING_16[
541	                        self.rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_16))]
542	                    buf[pos:pos + 2] = int(value & 0xFFFF).to_bytes(
543	                        2, "little" if op == 9 else "big")
544	            else:  # interesting 32-bit value, random endianness
545	                if len(buf) - pos >= 4:
546	                    value = INTERESTING_32[
547	                        self.rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_32))]
548	                    little = bool(self.rng.randint(0, 2))
549	                    buf[pos:pos + 4] = int(value & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(
550	                        4, "little" if little else "big")
551	            if len(buf) > self.max_input_len:
552	                del buf[self.max_input_len:]
553	        return bytes(buf)
554	
555	    def _havoc_stage(self, tc: TestCase, energy: int) -> None:
556	        """Havoc stage: `energy` iterations of stacked random mutations."""
557	        for _ in range(energy):
558	            self.evaluate(self._stack_havoc(tc.data), tc)
559	
560	    def _splice_stage(self, tc: TestCase, energy: int) -> None:
561	        """Splice stage: combine two queue entries at a midpoint, then
562	        run the result through havoc."""
563	        if len(self.queue) < 2:
564	            return
565	        for _ in range(energy):
566	            other = self.queue[self.rng.randint(0, len(self.queue))]
567	            if other is tc:
568	                continue
569	            mutant = splice(tc.data, other.data, self.rng)
570	            self.evaluate(self._stack_havoc(mutant), tc)
571	
572	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
573	    # Scheduling / main loop
574	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
575	
576	    def fuzz_one(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
577	        """Run the full AFL pipeline on one queue entry."""
578	        tc.times_chosen += 1
579	        tc.fuzz_count += 1
580	        if not tc.was_fuzzed:
581	            if self.enable_trimming:
582	                self.trim_case(tc)
583	            self._bitflip_stage(tc)
584	            self._byte_flip_stage(tc)
585	            self._arithmetic_stage(tc)
586	            self._interesting_stage(tc)
587	            self._dictionary_stage(tc)
588	            tc.was_fuzzed = True
589	        self.calculate_score(tc)
590	        self._havoc_stage(tc, self.assign_energy(tc))
591	        if self.current_cycle >= 1:
592	            self._splice_stage(tc, self.splice_energy)
593	
594	    def run(self, max_cycles: Optional[int] = None,
595	            max_execs: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
596	        """Main fuzzing loop.
597	
598	        Cycles through the queue in order; entries discovered during a
599	        cycle are scheduled from the next cycle onward. Non-favored seeds
600	        are skipped with probability ``skip_nonfavored_prob`` (75/25
601	        favored priority). The queue is re-culled after every cycle.
602	        """
603	        cycle = 0
604	        while max_cycles is None or cycle < max_cycles:
605	            self.current_cycle = cycle
606	            snapshot = list(self.queue)
607	            for tc in snapshot:
608	                if (max_execs is not None
609	                        and self.fork_server.exec_count >= max_execs):
610	                    self.cull_queue()
611	                    return
612	                has_favored = any(t.is_favored for t in self.queue)
613	                if (not tc.is_favored and has_favored
614	                        and self.rng.rand() < self.skip_nonfavored_prob):
615	                    continue
616	                self.fuzz_one(tc)
617	            self.cull_queue()
618	            cycle += 1

1	"""AFL (American Fuzzy Lop) core fuzzer simulation.
2	
3	A faithful reimplementation of AFL's core mechanisms on top of the fuzzsim
4	target model:
5	
6	- 64KB shared-memory bitmap with hit-count bucketing (``classify_counts``)
7	- edge coverage hashing via ``(prev_block XOR cur_block) >> 1``
8	- fork server simulation (``ForkServer``) with an execution counter
9	- test case calibration (multi-run stability detection, average exec time)
10	- input trimming (powers-of-two block removal preserving coverage)
11	- corpus culling via greedy set cover (smallest+fastest seed per edge)
12	- full deterministic stages in AFL order: walking bitflip 1/2/4 bits,
13	  byte flip 8/16/32 bits, arithmetic add/sub 1..35 for 8/16/32-bit widths
14	  (both endianness), interesting values 8/16/32 (both endianness),
15	  dictionary insertion (user tokens + auto-dictionary extracted during the
16	  bitflip stage when a byte value change produced new coverage)
17	- havoc stage with 2^1..2^7 stacked random mutations per iteration
18	- splice stage (midpoint combination of two queue entries, then havoc)
19	- performance scoring (``calculate_score``) from exec speed, coverage size,
20	  depth and stability
21	- constant power schedule (fixed energy per seed, AFL-style)
22	- crash deduplication via coverage hash (hash of the crashing edge set)
23	- queue scheduling with favored-seed priority (75% skip of non-favored
24	  seeds, 25% fuzz them anyway)
25	
26	All randomness flows through a single ``np.random.RandomState`` instance so
27	runs are fully deterministic given the seed.
28	"""
29	
30	import hashlib
31	from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
32	
33	import numpy as np
34	
35	from fuzzsim.bitmap import CoverageBitmap, MAP_SIZE
36	from fuzzsim.mutation import (
37	    INTERESTING_8,
38	    INTERESTING_16,
39	    INTERESTING_32,
40	    bit_flip,
41	    byte_flip,
42	    splice,
43	)
44	from fuzzsim.seed import TestCase
45	
46	ARITH_MAX = 35  # AFL arithmetic stage uses values 1..35
47	SKIP_NONFAVORED_PROB = 0.75  # 75% chance to skip a non-favored seed
48	CALIBRATION_RUNS = 3  # calibration executions per new test case
49	MAX_AUTO_DICT_TOKENS = 128  # cap on auto-extracted dictionary tokens
50	
51	# Interesting value tables per operand width (in bytes), as in AFL.
52	INTERESTING_BY_WIDTH = {
53	    1: INTERESTING_8,
54	    2: INTERESTING_16,
55	    4: INTERESTING_32,
56	}

59	def classify_counts(counts: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
60	    """Bucket raw hit counts the way AFL's ``classify_counts`` does.
61	
62	    Buckets: 1, 2, 3, 4-7, 8-15, 16-31, 32-127, 128+. Zero stays zero.
63	    The bucket id reported for a range is the range's lower bound encoded
64	    as in AFL's bucket shift table (1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 respectively).
65	    """
66	    counts = np.asarray(counts)
67	    out = np.zeros(counts.shape, dtype=np.uint8)
68	    out[counts == 1] = 1
69	    out[counts == 2] = 2
70	    out[counts == 3] = 3
71	    out[(counts >= 4) & (counts <= 7)] = 4
72	    out[(counts >= 8) & (counts <= 15)] = 5
73	    out[(counts >= 16) & (counts <= 31)] = 6
74	    out[(counts >= 32) & (counts <= 127)] = 7
75	    out[counts >= 128] = 8
76	    return out
77	
78	
79	def edge_hash(prev_block: int, cur_block: int) -> int:
80	    """Hash a CFG edge into the 64KB bitmap: (prev XOR cur) >> 1."""
81	    return ((prev_block ^ cur_block) >> 1) % MAP_SIZE

84	class ForkServerResult:
85	    """Result of a single fork-server execution."""
86	
87	    __slots__ = ("edges", "classified", "is_crash", "exec_time")
88	
89	    def __init__(self, edges: Set[int], classified: np.ndarray,
90	                 is_crash: bool, exec_time: float):
91	        self.edges = edges
92	        self.classified = classified  # bucketed 64KB bitmap (np.uint8 array)
93	        self.is_crash = is_crash
94	        self.exec_time = exec_time

97	class ForkServer:
98	    """Simulates AFL's fork server.
99	
100	    Executes the target on demand, keeps an execution counter, and reports
101	    coverage both as an exact edge set and as a classified 64KB bitmap
102	    (edge ids are mapped into the bitmap via ``edge_hash`` when the target
103	    exposes CFG block information, otherwise by edge id).
104	    """
105	
106	    def __init__(self, target):
107	        self.target = target
108	        self.exec_count = 0
109	        self._edge_index: Dict[int, int] = {}
110	        program = getattr(target, "program", None)
111	        if program is not None:
112	            for edge in program.edges:
113	                self._edge_index[edge.edge_id] = edge_hash(edge.src, edge.dst)
114	
115	    def bitmap_index(self, edge_id: int) -> int:
116	        """Return the bitmap index for an edge id."""
117	        return self._edge_index.get(edge_id, edge_id % MAP_SIZE)
118	
119	    def run(self, data: bytes) -> ForkServerResult:
120	        """Execute the target once and classify the hit counts."""
121	        self.exec_count += 1
122	        edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.target.execute(data)
123	        counts = np.zeros(MAP_SIZE, dtype=np.uint8)
124	        for edge_id in edges:
125	            idx = self.bitmap_index(edge_id)
126	            counts[idx] = min(255, counts[idx] + 1)
127	        return ForkServerResult(edges, classify_counts(counts),
128	                                is_crash, exec_time)

131	class AFLFuzzer:
132	    """Core AFL fuzzer driving a simulated target.
133	
134	    Parameters:
135	        target: program under test (must provide ``execute(bytes)``).
136	        seeds: initial corpus inputs.
137	        rng: ``np.random.RandomState`` used for ALL randomness.
138	        havoc_energy: fixed energy (havoc iterations) per scheduled seed;
139	            this is the constant power schedule.
140	        splice_energy: splice iterations per scheduled seed (from cycle 1).
141	        max_input_len: cap on mutated input length.
142	        enable_trimming: run powers-of-two trimming before deterministic
143	            stages (AFL default behavior; can be disabled per experiment).
144	        calibration_runs: executions per calibration.
145	        skip_nonfavored_prob: probability of skipping a non-favored seed.
146	    """
147	
148	    def __init__(self, target, seeds: List[bytes],
149	                 rng: Optional[np.random.RandomState] = None,
150	                 havoc_energy: int = 16, splice_energy: int = 4,
151	                 max_input_len: int = 1024, enable_trimming: bool = True,
152	                 calibration_runs: int = CALIBRATION_RUNS,
153	                 skip_nonfavored_prob: float = SKIP_NONFAVORED_PROB):
154	        self.target = target
155	        self.rng = rng if rng is not None else np.random.RandomState(0)
156	        self.havoc_energy = havoc_energy
157	        self.splice_energy = splice_energy
158	        self.max_input_len = max_input_len
159	        self.enable_trimming = enable_trimming
160	        self.calibration_runs = calibration_runs
161	        self.skip_nonfavored_prob = skip_nonfavored_prob
162	
163	        self.fork_server = ForkServer(target)
164	        self.bitmap = CoverageBitmap()
165	        # OR of all admitted classified bitmaps: a bucket pattern counts as
166	        # "new coverage" if it sets a byte never seen before.
167	        self._seen_classified = np.zeros(MAP_SIZE, dtype=np.uint8)
168	
169	        self.queue: List[TestCase] = []
170	        self.crashes: Dict[str, TestCase] = {}  # coverage hash -> crash TC
171	        self.user_dict: List[bytes] = []
172	        self.auto_dict: List[bytes] = []
173	        self.current_cycle = 0
174	        self.scores: Dict[int, float] = {}  # id(tc) -> calculate_score value
175	
176	        for seed in seeds:
177	            self._load_initial_seed(seed)
178	        self.cull_queue()
179	
180	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
181	    # Corpus / reporting properties
182	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
183	
184	    @property
185	    def paths_discovered(self) -> int:
186	        """Total number of queue entries (paths) discovered."""
187	        return len(self.queue)
188	
189	    @property
190	    def corpus_size(self) -> int:
191	        """Corpus size after culling bookkeeping (culling marks favored
192	        seeds but never removes entries, so this equals paths)."""
193	        return len(self.queue)
194	
195	    @property
196	    def unique_crashes(self) -> int:
197	        """Number of deduplicated crashes."""
198	        return len(self.crashes)
199	
200	    @property
201	    def exec_count(self) -> int:
202	        return self.fork_server.exec_count
203	
204	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
205	    # Calibration, trimming, culling
206	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
207	
208	    def calibrate_case(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
209	        """Run a test case multiple times to measure stability.
210	
211	        Stores the average execution time and flags the case as variable
212	        if the classified coverage differs between runs.
213	        """
214	        signatures = []
215	        times = []
216	        for _ in range(self.calibration_runs):
217	            res = self.fork_server.run(tc.data)
218	            signatures.append(res.classified.tobytes())
219	            times.append(res.exec_time)
220	        tc.exec_time = sum(times) / len(times) if times else 0.0
221	        # Dynamic attribute: TestCase has no stability field of its own.
222	        tc.is_variable = len(set(signatures)) > 1  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
223	
224	    def trim_case(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
225	        """Powers-of-two block removal trimming.
226	
227	        Try removing blocks of size len/2, len/4, ... down to 1 byte. A
228	        removal is kept only if the classified coverage is preserved.
229	        """
230	        data = tc.data
231	        if len(data) < 5:
232	            return
233	        reference = self.fork_server.run(data)
234	        if reference.is_crash:
235	            return
236	        ref_sig = reference.classified.tobytes()
237	
238	        shift = 1
239	        while (len(data) >> shift) >= 1:
240	            block = len(data) >> shift
241	            pos = 0
242	            while pos < len(data):
243	                end = min(pos + block, len(data))
244	                candidate = data[:pos] + data[end:]
245	                if candidate:
246	                    res = self.fork_server.run(candidate)
247	                    if (not res.is_crash
248	                            and res.classified.tobytes() == ref_sig):
249	                        data = candidate
250	                        continue  # retry at same position with shifted data
251	                pos += block
252	            shift += 1
253	        if data != tc.data:
254	            tc.data = data
255	
256	    def cull_queue(self) -> None:
257	        """Greedy set cover: for each covered edge pick the smallest and
258	        fastest queue entry covering it. Those entries are marked favored
259	        and their ``unique_edges`` set is updated."""
260	        best_for_edge: Dict[int, TestCase] = {}
261	        for edge_id in sorted(self.bitmap.global_coverage):
262	            best: Optional[TestCase] = None
263	            for tc in self.queue:
264	                if edge_id in tc.coverage:
265	                    if (best is None
266	                            or (tc.size, tc.exec_time) < (best.size,
267	                                                          best.exec_time)):
268	                        best = tc
269	            if best is not None:
270	                best_for_edge[edge_id] = best
271	
272	        favored = set(best_for_edge.values())
273	        for tc in self.queue:
274	            tc.is_favored = tc in favored
275	            tc.unique_edges = {e for e, b in best_for_edge.items() if b is tc}
276	
277	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
278	    # Scoring and power schedule
279	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
280	
281	    def calculate_score(self, tc: TestCase) -> float:
282	        """AFL-style performance score based on exec speed, coverage size,
283	        depth and stability. Higher is better."""
284	        if not self.queue:
285	            return 100.0
286	        avg_exec = sum(t.exec_time for t in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
287	        avg_cov = sum(len(t.coverage) for t in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
288	
289	        score = 100.0
290	        # Execution speed relative to the corpus average.
291	        if avg_exec > 0:
292	            ratio = tc.exec_time / avg_exec
293	            if ratio > 10:
294	                score *= 0.25
295	            elif ratio > 4:
296	                score *= 0.5
297	            elif ratio > 2:
298	                score *= 0.75
299	            elif ratio < 0.25:
300	                score *= 3.0
301	            elif ratio < 0.5:
302	                score *= 2.0
303	            elif ratio < 0.75:
304	                score *= 1.5
305	        # Coverage size relative to the corpus average.
306	        if avg_cov > 0:
307	            cratio = len(tc.coverage) / avg_cov
308	            if cratio > 3:
309	                score *= 4.0
310	            elif cratio > 2:
311	                score *= 3.0
312	            elif cratio > 1.5:
313	                score *= 2.0
314	            elif cratio < 0.25:
315	                score *= 0.25
316	            elif cratio < 0.5:
317	                score *= 0.5
318	            elif cratio < 0.75:
319	                score *= 0.75
320	        # Depth handicap: deeper inputs get less energy in AFL.
321	        if tc.depth > 3:
322	            score *= 0.8 ** min(tc.depth - 3, 8)
323	        # Stability: variable inputs are de-prioritized.
324	        if getattr(tc, "is_variable", False):
325	            score *= 0.5
326	
327	        self.scores[id(tc)] = score
328	        return score
329	
330	    def assign_energy(self, tc: TestCase) -> int:
331	        """Constant power schedule: every seed gets the same fixed energy."""
332	        return self.havoc_energy

334	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
335	    # Evaluation / queue admission / crash dedup
336	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
337	
338	    @staticmethod
339	    def crash_hash(edges: Set[int]) -> str:
340	        """Deduplication hash of a crashing edge set."""
341	        payload = ",".join(str(e) for e in sorted(edges)).encode()
342	        return hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
343	
344	    def _has_new_tuple(self, classified: np.ndarray) -> bool:
345	        """Check the classified bitmap for never-before-seen buckets."""
346	        return bool(np.any((classified > 0) & (self._seen_classified == 0)))
347	
348	    def _record_crash(self, data: bytes, res: ForkServerResult) -> bool:
349	        """Store a crash if its coverage hash has not been seen."""
350	        h = self.crash_hash(res.edges)
351	        if h in self.crashes:
352	            return False
353	        tc = TestCase(data=data, coverage=set(res.edges),
354	                      exec_time=res.exec_time, is_crash=True,
355	                      creation_time=self.fork_server.exec_count)
356	        self.crashes[h] = tc
357	        return True
358	
359	    def evaluate(self, data: bytes, parent: TestCase) -> bool:
360	        """Execute a candidate input; queue it on new coverage.
361	
362	        Crashes are deduplicated by coverage hash and never queued, but
363	        their coverage is folded into the global bitmap. Returns True if
364	        the input was added to the queue.
365	        """
366	        if not data:
367	            return False
368	        res = self.fork_server.run(data)
369	        if res.is_crash:
370	            self._record_crash(data, res)
371	            self.bitmap.update(res.edges)
372	            self._seen_classified |= res.classified
373	            return False
374	
375	        new_edges = res.edges - self.bitmap.global_coverage
376	        if not new_edges and not self._has_new_tuple(res.classified):
377	            return False
378	
379	        self.bitmap.update(res.edges)
380	        self._seen_classified |= res.classified
381	        tc = TestCase(
382	            data=data,
383	            coverage=set(res.edges),
384	            exec_time=res.exec_time,
385	            depth=parent.depth + 1,
386	            creation_time=self.fork_server.exec_count,
387	        )
388	        self.calibrate_case(tc)
389	        self.queue.append(tc)
390	        return True
391	
392	    def _load_initial_seed(self, data: bytes) -> None:
393	        """Add an initial seed to the queue (calibrated, deduplicating
394	        crashes). Like AFL, initial seeds are queued even if another seed
395	        already covers the same edges."""
396	        res = self.fork_server.run(data)
397	        self.bitmap.update(res.edges)
398	        self._seen_classified |= res.classified
399	        if res.is_crash:
400	            self._record_crash(data, res)
401	            return
402	        tc = TestCase(
403	            data=data,
404	            coverage=set(res.edges),
405	            exec_time=res.exec_time,
406	            depth=0,
407	            creation_time=self.fork_server.exec_count,
408	        )
409	        self.calibrate_case(tc)
410	        self.queue.append(tc)
